name: LBWIN Youth Career Services Center
org: City of Long Beach Economic Development and Opportunity, Workforce Development Bureau
what_you_do: Get free career help at a youth center: work-readiness workshops, help finding jobs, and paid internships or work experience such as Youth@Work.
who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 30. Youth@Work is for ages 14 to 24 and WIOA Youth services are listed for ages 16 to 24. WIOA funding focuses on out-of-school youth with barriers such as low income, foster care, homelessness, juvenile justice involvement, parenting, or a disability. A Long Beach residency rule is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Paid internships and Youth@Work (about 160 hours of paid work experience). Pay rates are not stated. Workshops and career help are free.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. The competitive school-to-career programs (Long Beach Public Service Corps, Port of Long Beach internship, Fire Corps internship and others) open for set application periods.
how_to_apply: Complete the Youth Interest Form on the city's Youth Services page. Partner agencies can also refer youth through the Unite Us platform.
notes: Because most WIOA funding targets youth facing barriers, a teen still in school may be steered to Youth@Work or a school-to-career program instead. Under 18 you need a California work permit for any paid placement. The city's Youth Opportunities page also lists teen volunteering at Long Beach libraries and at Parks, Recreation and Marine (ages 13 and up).
